messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT: runtime-gpu-1 / OOM events detected across 3 pods in us-west-2 (high severity). Pager sent to @anya (oncall) at 1912345678.
anya (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing a spike in OOMs reported by runtime-gpu-1. Attaching top-level summary: 3 pods, sustained OOMs over 2m, ~30% of requests 503.
anya (oncall): Quick customer impact check – SLOs failing for several mid-tier customers, particularly embeddings and chat endpoints. Notifying support.
sara-cs: Noted — we're seeing multiple customer error reports for embeddings endpoint, some retrying. Escalating to account owners for customers A and C.
matthew-r: Can someone dump recent dmesg / nvidia-smi logs? Hypothesis: fragmentation due to large kv-cache allocations + batch growth.
jing: Pasting short nvidia-smi snapshot and runtime logs (trimmed):
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-15T21:04:05Z
GPU0 memUsed: 15042 MiB / 16384 MiB
GPU1 memUsed: 15876 MiB / 16384 MiB
Processes: runtime-worker (pid 4123) kv_cache_alloc at 1.2GiB allocs, batch_size=32
OOM event recorded: out-of-memory: process killed
```

leo: Also found runtime logs with repeated `kv_cache_rebalance` entries and `eviction_failed` spikes.
leo: snippet: `kv_cache: free_pages=2, requested_pages=8, fragmentation_threshold=0.6, contiguous_alloc_failed`
anya (oncall): Immediate mitigations I can do now: 1) Force route new heavy requests to a fallback model smaller variant, 2) Temporarily cap max_batch_size to 16 at the gateway, 3) Drain the 3 affected pods for graceful restart. Which one should we do first?
dave-ml: Cap batch size first — that's low-risk and should reduce new pressure. Also suggest disabling prefix-KV caching for the embeddings route for short term (this lowers mem but may raise token cost).
ops-bot: Runbook step triggered: #oom-gpu -> scale up? Recommended: add 1 spare node before restart to avoid capacity loss.
anya (oncall): Executing step 2: updating gateway config to max_batch_size=16 for affected routes. Applying now.
(2 minutes pass)
anya (oncall): Gateway change applied. Observing drop in concurrent per-pod allocation attempts. OOMs still happening but rate decreased.
matthew-r: I'm pushing a quick patch to the runtime to lower `kv_cache_chunk_size` from 256MB to 128MB and reduce `cache_contiguous_alloc_limit` – will build and push to edge-canary.
jing: Shared a log bundle to the thread: https://internal.logs/redwood/incident/1912345678 — includes full OOM traces, heap maps, and `mallinfo` dumps.
leo: From the heap maps, fragmentation appears high: many small free regions spread across the 16GB range. Consequence: large contiguous allocations (required by some attention kernels) fail even with free total memory.
dave-ml: Hypothesis A: KV cache prefetch + a single large batch path triggers contiguous allocation failure when mem is fragmented. Hypothesis B: Recent autoscaler change allowed multiple high-batch inflight windows before backpressure.
anya (oncall): Customer impact note: Affected window ~21:03–21:11 UTC, ~8 minutes. Estimated 53 requests failed with 503, majority for embeddings heavy customers. Escalated to CS for service credits if SLA breach confirmed.
sara-cs: Copy. We're drafting outreach and will wait for final window confirmation.
ops-bot: Suggested live mitigation: 1) Drain two pods to force reallocation to fresh nodes, 2) Add one warm spare node, 3) Toggle `kv_cache.enabled=false` for embeddings route via feature flag if pressure persists.
anya (oncall): Starting drain on pod runtime-gpu-1a then runtime-gpu-1b. Creating spare node now.
(4 minutes pass)
anya (oncall): Drains complete. Spare node added and new pods scheduled on fresh nodes. OOM events stopped within 90s of new pods being ready.
matthew-r: Canary build passed with reduced chunk size — running it on a single canary pod to validate contiguous allocation behavior.
jing: Noted a pattern in timeline: 21:02 – Model rollout of v2.3.1 with a change to batch_window_ms=45 landed 2m before incident. Might be contributing.
dave-ml: Good catch. If batch_window increased, effective batch sizes could spike under bursty traffic. That + kv prefetch likely pushed fragmentation.
leo: Long-term remediation suggestions: 1) Add contiguous allocator heuristics or slab for attention kernel allocations, 2) Make kv_cache allocation less contiguous-dependent (chunking + scatter), 3) Add runtime backpressure for in-flight large batches when fragmentation detected, 4) Add a canary check for memory fragmentation on rollout.
anya (oncall): For the post-incident checklist: collect heap maps from affected nodes, snapshot scheduler decisions, audit the rollout at 21:02, and prepare a customer-impact timeline. Assigning tasks: heap maps -> jing, rollout audit -> matthew-r, customer comms -> sara-cs, runtime followups -> dave-ml + leo.
matthew-r: Will also revert batch_window_ms change in the next patch if can reproduce load -> fragmentation locally.
sara-cs: Customer comms drafted and awaiting final numbers. Will send targeted notes to impacted customers within the hour.
anya (oncall): Incident status: mitigation successful, system stabilized. Opening a formal RCA ticket and marking P1 -> P2 for follow-up. Will hand off to dave-ml for deep-dive. Next on-call: @leo in 30m; handing off now.
leo: Taking handoff. I'll coordinate RCA writeup and schedule infra change for canary fragmentation checks.
ops-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 1912345899.
anya (oncall): Thanks team — excellent fast mitigation. We'll include the batch_window rollback and kv cache config changes in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
